_comment: Q26 pilot: does the model use render_table's richer column types when the data calls for them? One prompt per rarely used type or option, data in the prompt, no type named. best, haiku, n=5. Registered before the run.
headline: The menu works when the data calls for it: sparkline, trend, image and boolean 5/5, search 5/5, progress 4/5 (the fifth a percentage). They were absent from the 227 earlier tables because those questions never called for them, not because they are unreachable.

Two types are passed over for a simpler form: a 1–6 condition score went to a coloured badge 5/5, never rating; a list of installations per building went to a text cell 5/5, never multi_badge. A status symbol went to badge 3/5 and icon 1/5; the schema itself calls badge the type for a status.

Link and footer lose runs to form, not type: 2 link and 3 footer runs answered in text or a markdown table without calling render_table. Every drawn table used the target: link 3/3, footer 2/2. One icon run declined the question as outside the building domain.
No render_table call was refused (0 of 54).

predictions.P1: HOLDS — 10 of 12 paths reach the target or an alternative in ≥ 3/5 (not multi_badge 0/5, footer 2/5).
predictions.P3: FALSIFIED on footer — 2/5, because 3 runs drew no table; badge 5/5.

what_follows: No guidance split for render_table: the rarer types are reached when the data calls for them, so the question would be cost alone (about 2.6k of 7.9k characters, a few percent per run after a guidance tool's own entry). rating and multi_badge are passed over for forms that read as well (a coloured badge, a text list); not a defect on this data.

log_audit.note: render_table rows now carry columnTypes, footers and features in shape.
